title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — mass-priest analogy: switching persons same moment (sin loco, punish suo)
pass_a_gloss: Same title and same moment of punishment—unless you invent a mass-priest switch of persons: Adam representing us when sinning, sustaining only himself when punished, nearly at once. Placeus treats that costume-change as the only escape hatch.
pass_b_english: Ought he not to have been punished under the same title under which he sinned, especially at the same moment? Unless you mean that, as a pontifical priest celebrating mass puts on Christ's person and then puts it off, and so plays different persons in almost the same moment, so Adam likewise sometimes represented our person, sometimes sustained his own alone—and in the same moment both sinned in our place and was punished in his own, not ours.
source_text: Annon quo nomine peccavit eodem puniri debuit, praesertim eodem momento? nisi velis, quemadmodum sacrificulus pontificius inter celebrandum missam modo Christi personam induit, modo deponit, atque ita diversas agit personas eodem paene momento, sic Adamum similiter modo personam nostram repraesentasse, modo suam unius sustinuisse, atque eodem momento & peccasse loco nostro, & punitum suo, non nostro.

lemmas.gloss: punished in his own, not ours

notes: Cap. IX missa/poena densify section 642 from locked 1661 Latin (pp. 354–355 tip).
